title: PRD: Adaptive Output Profiles for Multi-Mode Hosted Endpoints + Launch Safeguards
creator: Ava Morales
description: Purpose: Define and ship Adaptive Output Profiles for the unified hosted inference surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). These profiles let product teams and customers pick runtime behavioral modes (e.g., high-consistency, low-latency, cost-optimized) while ensuring clear acceptance criteria, telemetry, and safe launch/rollback controls. This ticket is the PRD + launch safeguards checklist for implementation and go/no-go readiness.
goals: Deliver a server-side mechanism to select an 'Output Profile' per request or per endpoint that adjusts model selection, temperature defaults, decoding constraints, and fallback policies.
Provide a documented set of 3 initial profiles: Consistent, Responsive, and Economical, each with clear behavioral guarantees and cost/latency trade-offs.
Wire platform controls to enforce profile-specific SLAs and automated graded fallbacks (e.g., degrade to cheaper model variant when latency SLO is at risk).
Create launch-grade telemetry, regressions alerts, and runbooks for safe canary and regional rollouts.
in_scope: API: add optional 'output_profile' field to request payloads for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank and SDKs.
Runtime: routing policy hooks to select model variant, quantization profile, and decoding params based on profile.
Console: per-endpoint dropdown to default output_profile and per-route override controls.
Telemetry: profile-tagged metrics, quality regressions (eval sets), latency/cost breakdowns, and alert rules.
out_of_scope: New profile creation UI for customers (post-launch feature).
Per-tenant custom kernel selection or hardware placement controls (reserved for Dedicated).
Automated prompt rewriting for profile-level behavioral adjustments (future work).
requirements: API contract: optional string field 'output_profile' (allowed: 'consistent','responsive','economical') and opaque 'profile_version' for future compatibility.
Default behavior: if missing, platform uses account default; if account default missing, platform sets 'responsive'.
Runtime behavior mapping: each profile maps to model family, temperature cap, token-sampling strategy, top_p/top_k heuristics, KV cache retention policy, and batching aggressiveness.
Fallbacks: when profile's latency SLO is violated, rollback to profile-tiered variants per policy with observable trace logs and reason codes.
Console: visibility into per-profile P95 latency, cost-per-1k-tokens, quality score (from evaluation prompts), and recent regressions.
acceptance_criteria: API validation: requests with invalid 'output_profile' return 400 with a documented error code.
Runtime selection: end-to-end test harness demonstrates that each profile routes to distinct model/decoding config at least 90% of the time across traffic shapes.

Latency & cost: for synthetic telco workload (specified in artifacts) 'responsive' must hit P95 < 200ms for short sequences; 'economical' must show >=15% cost reduction vs responsive for the same throughput under load tests.
Quality: on the canonical eval set, 'consistent' must not regress BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity by more than 2% vs baseline; automated evaluation runs are added to CI.
Observability: profile tag present in 100% of telemetry, dashboards correctly filter by profile, and alerting rules fire on SLI breaches during canary.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Internal alpha: route 100% of internal staging traffic through profiles; gather eval and SLO metrics.
Stage 1 - Canary (10%): enable for 10% of production traffic on non-critical accounts; monitor for 72 hours.
Stage 2 - Gradual increase (10% -> 50% -> 100%): increase in 4 increments with 24-72 hour guardrails; automated rollback if critical alerts fire.
Stage 3 - Tenant opt-in GA: expose console toggle to customers; keep platform default as 'responsive' until customer opt-in is >25% across active users.
launch_checklist: PRs merged: API schema, SDK updates (python/js), runtime selection hooks, console visibility, and canary orchestration PRs all merged and green.
Security: KMS review concluded for any profile-specific key access; security sign-off recorded in ticket comments.
E2E tests: automated E2E tests covering each profile behavior added to CI and passing for runtime-1.22 branch.
Telemetry: dashboards created and accessible to SRE/product; alert thresholds set and test alerts exercised.
Canary playbook: documented playbook with exact rollback commands, owner on-call list, and escalation timeline in Confluence.
Customer comms: release notes drafted and staged, and sample default-language snippets for migration guide included.
telemetry_and_alerting: SLIs: P95 latency per profile, error rate < 0.5% for GA accounts, and infra OOM/CPU pressure per model-variant.
Alerts: automatic rollback alarm if profile.p95_latency increases >30% over baseline for 3 consecutive 5m windows or if error_rate >1%.
Quality regression detection: nightly eval job compares baseline eval set; if embedding similarity drops >3% or generation score delta >5% the quality-alert triggers on-call.
dependencies: ENG-4510: SDK schema upgrade for optional profile field
ENG-4782: console per-endpoint feature flags and defaults
PM-710999: behavioral contract PRD (alignment on definitions)
SRE-212: alert-onboarding and pager duty mapping
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: subtle quality regressions when using cost-optimized model variants. Mitigation: nightly eval with canary gating and manual rollback if quality-alert fires.
Risk: profile tags leak into user-visible output or tokens affecting downstream billing. Mitigation: ensure profile metadata is not surfaced in generated outputs and add billing tests.
Risk: operator confusion on defaults. Mitigation: clear console copy, example requests, and migration guide; require confirmation on console toggle to change account default.

notes_for_engineers: Ensure 'profile_version' is included in traces for future migrations; runtime should tolerate unknown profile_version by falling back to 'responsive'.
Do not alter public API surface for existing clients if field not provided; keep backward compatibility guaranteed.
Add synthetic load tests that mimic bursty small-sequence chat traffic as well as long-sequence completion workloads.
